clue.text: Music prone to blast in theatrical feature

indicators.note: to blast something is to blow it apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Loud music liable to blare out during a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music' and 'prone' look like the subject of the sentence, but together they are just the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The proscenium is the arch framing the stage opening in a traditional theatre, a standard architectural part of the building.

clue.text: Servant's sheet

blocks.note: first meaning: a boy attendant in a household or hotel
second meaning: one leaf of paper in a book

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like a sheet belonging to a servant; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A young attendant or messenger boy has this title, and a single leaf of a book or document carries the same name.

clue.text: Brown bread, unopened oven

indicators.note: something unopened is missing its opening, so the front letter goes

blocks.note: toast is bread browned under heat

explanation.surface: A loaf of brown bread sitting in an oven whose door was never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bread' reads as wholemeal, but here it means bread that has been browned. An oast is a kiln, a sense of oven common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of heated chamber, so it counts as an oven in the broad sense.

clue.text: Perhaps Chad irons (perhaps) in leisure centres

blocks.note: Chad is an example of a nation in central Africa
irons are an example of golf clubs

explanation.surface: Someone named Chad does the ironing at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Chad and irons look like a man and his laundry, but each is an example of a category: the African state and the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Country clubs are private establishments offering sports and social facilities, which makes them places of recreation.

clue.text: Naturalised American - Vladimir, initially - harbouring troublesome book?

definitions.text: Naturalised American - Vladimir, initially - harbouring troublesome book?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each preceding word is kept
something troublesome is unruly and disordered, so its letters are rearranged
to harbour is to give shelter, so one set of letters takes in another

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a Russian-born writer who became a US citizen and wrote a scandalous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: Vladimir Nabokov became an American citizen, and his 'troublesome book' is Lolita.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov, the Russian-born novelist, took US citizenship and wrote Lolita, a famously controversial novel.

clue.text: Disregarded some fun (not educational)

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters are just a part of the following words

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: Fun that isn't educational gets ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make the words look like an aside, but the answer runs straight through them: f-UN NOT ED-ucational.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnoticed or ignored has not been remarked upon, a straightforward synonym for passed over.

clue.text: Apostles' contribution to Scripture, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the leading letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the leading letters of the four words

explanation.surface: What the apostles added to the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the Acts of the Apostles is the New Testament book recording their deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is the fifth book of the New Testament, describing the early church's deeds.

clue.text: Key groups including four subordinate to American Navy Seals?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being subordinate means sitting lower, so one piece is placed underneath another
to include is to take inside, so one set of letters goes within the other

blocks.note: a core is a key or central group
A is the abbreviation for American
RN is the Royal Navy
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Key teams of elite US Navy SEAL special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navy Seals' reads as the US special-forces unit, but Navy is wordplay and Seals is the definition, with the question mark flagging an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals eat fish and other animals, so they are an example of meat-eating mammals, belonging to the order Carnivora.

clue.text: Proxy – but it set us up

indicators.note: up can mean astir or in turmoil, as when things are up in the air, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: the letters of these words, with set doing double service

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a proxy vote was a trap: it framed us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set us up' reads as a complaint about being framed; 'set' is part of the letters, and only 'up' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is someone authorised to act in another person's place, which is what a stand-in or replacement does.

clue.text: Performing, a singer – but one full of hot air?

indicators.note: performing means putting on an act, so the letters take on a new form

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A singer performing well enough, but a windbag full of empty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of hot air' is the idiom for a boaster, which fits a singer; read literally it describes an engine driven by hot gases.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas turbine is an engine powered by hot combusted gases spinning blades, so it is literally filled with heated air.

clue.text: Gloomy poet retires

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A melancholy poet goes off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retires' suggests going to bed or giving up work; here it means the word goes backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull, dreary and lacking in colour or cheer, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Awareness Tom displayed in former sovereign state

indicators.note: something displayed is laid out for show, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A man called Tom showed political awareness in a country that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pacific nation was renamed simply Samoa in 1997, which is why its old name counts as a former state.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Samoa was the official name of the independent Pacific island country until 1997, when it dropped the compass point.

clue.text: Absorb costs: that includes unspecified amount, if you catch my drift

definitions.note: the clue's 'if you catch my drift' becomes 'if you take the hint'

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to take the hit is to absorb a financial loss
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A knowing aside about someone covering the bills, plus a bit extra.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the algebraic symbol for an indefinite number, a regular crossword source for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand an implied meaning without it being spelt out is what both phrases describe; they are idiomatic equivalents.

clue.text: Examples of teamwork when party line's neglected

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disarray, so its letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of the words, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Politicians cooperate well once they stop following the official party policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party line' reads as political doctrine; here it is ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Interplay is the cooperative give-and-take between colleagues or players, so instances of it show joint effort.

clue.text: Bachelor explored book about odd British component of Scotch egg

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
to have read a book is to have explored it
C is short for circa, Latin for about
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A single man looked through a book about a strange British snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British picnic food: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and coated in crumbs before frying.
explanation.definitionFit: The crispy coating on a Scotch egg is made of tiny fragments of dried loaf, each one a small part of it.

clue.text: Thoroughbred who defected to the West?

blocks.note: first meaning: a champion racehorse of the 1980s bearing this name
second meaning: the Soviet ballet star who sought asylum in Paris in 1961

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thoroughbred' seems to praise the dancer's pedigree, but it points to a racehorse named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev, the Russian ballet dancer, escaped the Soviet Union in 1961, and a famous racehorse was named after him.

clue.text: Michigan city right to take in alien

indicators.note: to take in is to admit or receive, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: droit is a legal right, from French
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A city in Michigan is entitled to admit foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' suggests an immigrant; it is the extraterrestrial ET. Droit survives in English legal language for a right or due.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the largest city in the US state of Michigan, famous for the car industry and Motown music.

clue.text: Gave power to English knight, one that's exhausted

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
N is the knight in chess notation
a means one
bled dry means drained or exhausted

explanation.surface: A worn-out English knight is granted authority.
explanation.walkthrough: N is used for a knight because K is already taken by the king in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the means or authority to do something is to empower them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Covered in hair, suffused with bad smell: steady on!

indicators.note: to be suffused with something is to be filled through by it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: downy means covered in fine soft hair
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A smelly hairy dog is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, short for body odour, is a common crossword source for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The command given to an overexcited dog is a way of telling it to calm down, the same as urging restraint.

clue.text: Bobby, we're told, is a portraitist

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a bobby is a British policeman, and a sergeant is a police rank

explanation.surface: A policeman turns out to be a painter of portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer; a sergeant is one rank of bobby.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was an American painter famed for society portraits, notably Madame X.

clue.text: Wickedness overcoming the French pastor, model lingered in bed

indicators.note: to overcome is to get on top of and surround, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: sin is wickedness
le is French for the
P is a dictionary abbreviation for pastor
the Model T was the classic Ford car

explanation.surface: A sinful French clergyman and a model stay in bed late.
explanation.walkthrough: Model T, the early Ford car, is how T comes from 'model'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in bed past the usual time of rising is a dawdle under the covers, the meaning of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: They're fast sportspeople, despite business attire

blocks.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to, used when disagreeing
bowler hats were traditional City business wear

explanation.surface: Athletes who are quick in spite of wearing suits.
explanation.walkthrough: Pace bowlers are cricketers who deliver the ball fast; bowlers are also the round hard hats once worn by London businessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the quick deliverers of the ball are called by this name, as opposed to spinners.

clue.text: Comfy spot Francis of Assisi hides

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it concealed inside, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: The saint has a cosy hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Francis, all of 'of' and the start of Assisi.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is an upholstered seat for lounging, a comfortable place to sit at home.

clue.text: Rum, perhaps? Reportedly, Everyman will

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I will, contracted

explanation.surface: A setter offers to have a glass of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, not the drink; the setter refers to themselves as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a Scottish island, so it is an example of an island, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Lean on musical instrument, keeling over

indicators.note: something keeling over turns upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone props themselves on an instrument and it topples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean on' looks like an instruction to rest on the instrument; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To border or rest against something adjoining is to touch it at the edge, the sense of the verb.

clue.text: 'Restrained'? Sadly, I mess about

indicators.note: something done sadly is done badly, so the letters come out wrongly arranged

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone told to behave admits that sadly they fool around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess about' looks like the anagram signal, but 'about' is part of the letters; 'Sadly' does the signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means moderate in eating and drinking, showing self-control, so it is a synonym for holding back.

clue.text: 'Help!', bishop stifled howls

indicators.note: to be stifled is to be smothered or covered up, so one piece is wrapped inside another

blocks.note: SOS is the distress signal
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cry for help as a bishop muffles someone's wailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stifled howls' reads as muffled cries; 'stifled' belongs with bishop, which is smothered by the distress call.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe loud crying or weeping, so as plural nouns they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Resting on a streak of foamy water is worrying

blocks.note: lying down is resting

blocks.clueFragment: on a streak of foamy water
blocks.note: a wake is the foamy trail left by a boat, and 'on' simply joins it after the first piece

explanation.surface: Floating on a ship's frothy trail is a cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting' and 'worrying' seem opposed, but someone lying awake at night is doing both.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to sleep because of anxiety is the image the phrase conjures, so it stands for fretting.
